exposure: Multimodal pain power plan (standard therapeutic postpartum activity goals, tiered order sets with scheduled NSAIDs, embedded changes in electronic health record)
outcome: Hospital Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (HCAHPS) pain management scores
cohort: Women who delivered at 5 hospitals in Central Texas
finding: Implementation of a standardized multimodal pain power plan led to a significant reduction in opioid use among women admitted to labor and delivery, though some women reported increased pain despite achieving functional goals.
mod_finding: The risk of opioid use decreased by 26% among women who delivered vaginally and 18% among women who delivered by cesarean after the implementation of the pain power plan.
